protocol: Daylight Share Lab (reader-experiment/share/LAB-PROTOCOL.md) on protocol v1, revision 1.1
notes: Everything here is deterministic: CI regenerates this file and requires no diff. Secrets are those of test-vectors.json (pairing[0] is vector-secret-1). Times: `time` is a relay time in Unix seconds, `now`, `at`, `poll` and `checkedIn` are milliseconds since 1970 (UTC), and a state's `t` is Unix seconds.
loneSurrogates: the case holds a UTF-16 lone surrogate (written as a \ud800 escape). Swift skips these cases (Swift strings cannot hold one); JS and Kotlin run them.
constants: the Lab constants every port uses (2.2, 2.7.2).

labTopics: the four derived topics (2.4) for each secret: "dls-" + the first 32 hex digits of SHA-256(label + 0x00 + secret). aads: the AAD of every purpose; an unknown purpose is an error ("purpose"), never a default. returnFrame: seal headerJson bytes with the pairing key, nonceHex and the lab-return AAD; it must equal frameHex, open back, and fail to open (an error "frame") with each of refusedPurposes.

labFrames: Lab frames (2.2.1) sealed like acks (pairing key of vector-secret-1, AAD dlshare/v1/ack). Seal headerJson bytes with nonceHex: the frame must equal frameBase64; open it and run parseLabAck: it must equal `parse`. headerBytes, frameLength and base64Length pin the worst case of 2.2.1 (2,572, 2,608 and 3,480), and every frame is small. A builder (buildLabFrame / LabFrame.build) refuses more than 24 states and any frame that is not small.

labParse: parse headerJson with the platform JSON parser; a parse failure, or anything that is not an object, is step 1 of 2.2.5. Then parseLabAck must give expect exactly: inbox null or {lab, app, caps, poll (ms or null), live}, and states [{id, s, t}] in order. Rule I (integers by value: 1.0, 1e0 and 0.1e1 are 1, -0 is 0, "1", true and 1.5 are not), rule D (dates checked field by field, ASCII digits only) and the clamps are all exercised.

labLedger: feed each step (headerJson parsed, relay `time` in seconds) to LabLedger.record in order, then read the ledger at `now`: states (for the ids that have one), inboxLab, caps (the union of fresh publishers with lab >= 1, sorted), hasCap per token, checkedIn (the later of heard and the newest clamped poll, or null) and publishers (android, reader-lab or other: lab, app, caps, poll clamped to its message's relay time, live, at). A publisher is fresh while now - at <= 36 h. A message replaces its publisher's entry when its at is the same or later. A header whose kind is not "ack" is ignored, heard included.

labGate: build the gate's ctx from the stub: lab, paired, caps (hasCap is true for these tokens), local (the app's own check answers this state), server (null: no server object; {state, message}: what server.state(key) answers; "never": it never answers, so the gate's deadline gives OFFLINE; "throws-offline": it throws an OFFLINE error whose message is the OFFLINE text), serverMessages (the server module's texts, for an OFFLINE the deadline decided), built (absent = built) and platform. expect: ready, state, message, short, button, and serverKey (the key server.state was asked for, or null). Run "never" with a short deadline in tests; the real one is GATE_DEADLINE_MS.

labHeaderExtras: checkItemHeader (ItemHeader.check) of headerJson must succeed and its extras must equal expect: x-cap when it is seen, clean, excerpt or test; x-orig when it passes the web URL rule (the trimmed value; receivers do not apply the sender's 1,024-character limit); both from part 0 only; every other x- field dropped.

labRowText: describeLabRow(row, now, ctx) (LabRowText) must equal expect.label, sentence, action (null, "retry-now" or "try-again"), stepLine (null for v1.1 rows) and final; expect.a11y is the row's accessibility label ("{label}. {sentence}"). ctx.hasCap is the list of tokens for which hasCap is true; ctx.state is {s, t}, a bare token or null; ctx.online false means offline.

labText: strings is LAB_TEXT flattened to dotted ids (arrays joined with ","); every app shows exactly these. messages: needsMessage(state, {platform, feature, short, heading, message}) -> expect (null = no text of its own: the server module's text is used). checkedIn: checkedInText(ms, now). inboxHeader: the What's in Lab header line. features: the name and sentence of each Lab feature, in list order (the four server features last). serverRow: the server's state for the whole server -> heading (serverHeadingShort: the line under What's in Lab's server heading; needs-server is "Not set up"; an unknown state is error) and subtitle (serverRowSubtitle: the "Daylight server ›" row, "Optional · {short}" with that heading form). serverFeature: serverFeatureShort(state, headingState) -> a server feature row's own short state, or null when its state equals the heading's (unknown states count as error). serverSection (2.6, the Daylight server section): moved: serverMovedText(moved) fills {host} with discover()'s new origin minus its scheme and any path, as text (the port stays); labInboxSeen: labInboxSeenText(lastSeen, now) with GET /v1/status's inbox.lastSeen (an ISO time read by rule D, or ms; anything else is the not-yet line); aiToday: aiTodayText(used, cap), where an amount is n × 100 in double precision rounded half up to cents (so 1.005 is "1" and 0.015 is "0.02"; never printf or toFixed), ".00" left out, and anything but a finite number above 0 is "0".

v1Safety: each labFrames frame as a v1.0 or v1.1 ack reader sees it: it opens as an ack whose ids are [], so it acks nothing and no row changes. Kotlin's AckHeader.idsOf and Swift's AckHeader.ids(in:) must return [] for each.

W1 (L1; LAB-PROTOCOL 2.9). normalise.json holds smart intake (F16). labText also has: kindLines (inboxKindLine: the line under an Inbox row, F03), cleanedFrom (cleanedFromText(orig): "Cleaned from {host}" or null), use (labUseOn(settings, feature): Lab on and the feature's Use switch not off; a missing key is on) and useFeatures (the features with a Use switch, their footers and the switch's accessibility label).

labExcerpt (F11): items: excerptItem(input) -> the item to send ({kind, mime, name, url?, title, content, extras}) or null; sanitize: sanitizeExcerptHtml(html, maxChars) -> {html, trimmed}; textHtml: excerptTextHtml(text, maxChars); fragments: textFragment(url, text) (null for a URL that fails the web URL rule); dates: excerptDate(date) ("" when the date is not a valid YYYY-MM-DD); fileNames: excerptFileName(text, {note}); classify: classifyShare(input) -> {kind, url, text} (6.5 Q1 = b: rules 1-3 only); limits: the input text is textRepeat repeated `times` times, then trimmed; excerptItem (text alone, and with html "

" + text + "

") and excerptMarkdown must give a content of `length` UTF-16 units with that SHA-256 (of its UTF-8) and that ending.

diagnostics (F26): redact: redactDiagnostics(text) -> expect; activity: activityEvent(input) -> event, activityLine(event) -> line; reports: diagnosticsReport(input) -> expect (input.now is the clock for the check-in's relative time).
testArticle (F26): testArticle({id, device}) -> the item to send ({id, kind, url, title, content, extras}).

ids not empty: Lab fields ignored
x-st elements that are not objects
the same i twice: both, in order
poll on Feb 29 of a leap year (2028)
poll on Feb 29, 2100 (not leap: divisible by 100)
poll with one fraction digit (.5 = 500 ms)
poll with two fraction digits (.05 = 50 ms)
poll with an offset instead of Z
poll with lowercase t and z
poll with a space instead of T
lab 2 (above LAB_LEVEL): the whole frame is unknown

labLedger.name: a v1.1 ack only: heard, no Lab
a hello: Lab on, its caps, checked in at poll or heard
equal rank with a later t replaces
equal rank with an earlier t is ignored
equal rank and equal t: the first stays
a lower rank is ignored
held after waiting, then a re-announced waiting
repeats of an id within one frame merge in order
a hello exactly 36 h old is still fresh
a hello gone stale at 36 h + 1 ms
two publishers, android first: caps are the union
two publishers, reader-lab first: caps are the union
two publishers within the same relay second
the same publisher twice in one relay second: the later message wins
an older message after a newer one is ignored
lab 0 from one of two publishers
lab 0 from the only publisher ends Lab at once
handover 5.3.4: Daylight Share hands over to the Lab Reader
handover back: the Lab Reader stops, Daylight Share receives again
a poll later than its relay time is clamped
heard later than the newest poll
states without x-inbox are kept; no Lab
an unknown or empty app is the publisher other
a later Lab level is ignored, but heard
a header whose kind is not ack is ignored

strings.testArticle.title: Test article from {device}
strings.testArticle.heading: A test article from Send to Daylight
strings.testArticle.p1: This short article was sent by Setup check in Send to Daylight. If you are reading it on your Daylight, the whole path works: your device sealed it, the relay carried it, Daylight Share on your Daylight opened it, and the Reader saved it to your library. Nothing in it needs the network, so it reads the same with Wi-Fi off.
strings.testArticle.p2: It is written to be long enough that the Reader keeps it as a page of its own. Very short pages make the Reader fetch the address again, and the address of this article leads nowhere on purpose: it ends in .invalid, a name that never resolves. So if you see this text, it came through Send to Daylight and not from the web.
strings.testArticle.p3: Back on the device you sent it from, Setup check follows the article along its way. It ticks Delivered when your Daylight confirms that the item arrived, and In your Reader when the Reader says that it saved it. If your Daylight asks before it opens new items, the check waits until you tap the notice there, and says so in the meantime.
strings.testArticle.p4: You can send a test article whenever something seems wrong, for example after you change your Wi-Fi, update an app or pair again. Each one has a new address, so the Reader never mistakes one for another, and each one shows up as a new item in your library. When the checks look right, you are ready to send pages, links and documents for real.
strings.testArticle.p5: A few things are worth knowing while you are here. Pages you send go as you saw them, logged-in parts included, but without scripts or anything you typed into forms. Links you send are cleaned of tracking first. And items you share while offline wait on your device and go as soon as it is back online.
strings.testArticle.p6: When you are done, delete this article in the Reader, as you would delete anything else you read. Deleting it changes nothing in Send to Daylight or in Daylight Share, and sending another test article later works just as this one did. Thank you for trying the Lab version of Send to Daylight.

expect.title: Test article from Anjan’s iPhone
expect.content:
A test article from Send to Daylight

This short article was sent by Setup check in Send to Daylight. If you are reading it on your Daylight, the whole path works: your device sealed it, the relay carried it, Daylight Share on your Daylight opened it, and the Reader saved it to your library. Nothing in it needs the network, so it reads the same with Wi-Fi off.

It is written to be long enough that the Reader keeps it as a page of its own. Very short pages make the Reader fetch the address again, and the address of this article leads nowhere on purpose: it ends in .invalid, a name that never resolves. So if you see this text, it came through Send to Daylight and not from the web.

Back on the device you sent it from, Setup check follows the article along its way. It ticks Delivered when your Daylight confirms that the item arrived, and In your Reader when the Reader says that it saved it. If your Daylight asks before it opens new items, the check waits until you tap the notice there, and says so in the meantime.

You can send a test article whenever something seems wrong, for example after you change your Wi-Fi, update an app or pair again. Each one has a new address, so the Reader never mistakes one for another, and each one shows up as a new item in your library. When the checks look right, you are ready to send pages, links and documents for real.

A few things are worth knowing while you are here. Pages you send go as you saw them, logged-in parts included, but without scripts or anything you typed into forms. Links you send are cleaned of tracking first. And items you share while offline wait on your device and go as soon as it is back online.

When you are done, delete this article in the Reader, as you would delete anything else you read. Deleting it changes nothing in Send to Daylight or in Daylight Share, and sending another test article later works just as this one did. Thank you for trying the Lab version of Send to Daylight.
